annotationRationale: Both routes condition on the next jump and use reflection symmetry. The main route determines neighboring probabilities directly; the alternative constructs and solves first-step equations without relying on diagonal exit symmetry.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Under the intended equally likely four directions, the vertical-exit probability is 5/8, choice B. A corner cannot be the first boundary point, so vertical and horizontal exits do not overlap. No statement, choice or figure contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful reference routes are retained: diagonal path symmetry and first-step probability equations. Each independently yields the answer.
review.annotationCheck: The state/first-step node is appropriate, especially for the equation method. Total probability and reflection support both routes; complementarity and algebraic elimination are accurately method-specific additions.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: From any interior point, three left choices force exit, giving survival probability at most (63/64)^k after k blocks and hence eventual termination. The stated diagonal reflections preserve path probabilities and exchange the two exit types. Thus the three non-left first moves each give success probability 1/2, yielding 1/4+(3/4)(1/2)=5/8.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 1 through 3 support the first-jump symmetry route. The candidate adds independently written path pairing, termination and corner arguments. Its attribution correctly identifies a nonofficial source-informed original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The reflection axes and their effects are specified, so no diagram is necessary. The elementary survival bound and corner observation justify why equal exit probabilities must each be 1/2.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The state node fits the current-position and first-step reduction, closed immediately by symmetry. cnm_h246 matches the weighted first-jump cases, cnm_132 the geometric reflections, and cnm_h139 the exhaustive, mutually exclusive exit types.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native total-probability, reflection and complementary-event links support the stated steps. Geometric reflection alone does not establish probability symmetry; the candidate explicitly supplies the path-pairing argument. The state node has no supplied CN alignment.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: Reflection and length preservation give partial overlap with 8.G.A.1a and G-CO.B.6. The angle/parallel-line tasks in 8.G.A.1b/c, experimental verification in 8.G.A.1, and transformation-function work in G-CO.A.2 are not demonstrated. No US links are supplied for the probability nodes.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All four immediate IDs are supported. The state node is used through first-step analysis rather than a recursive linear system; reflection and complementarity provide the closing probabilities.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The reflections correctly reduce all nine interior points to four states. Each displayed equation matches its four neighbors and absorbing-side values. Subtraction gives x-y=1/4; substitution gives 4y=3/4+2y, hence y=3/8 and x=5/8. These equations apply to eventual vertical success without requiring a separate termination assumption.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solutions 4 and 5 support the state equations. The shorter elimination is independently presented, and the sourceMethod description accurately identifies the source contribution and modification. No official MAA provenance is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The sufficient state information, symmetry classes, boundary values and averaging rule are explained. The representative neighbor example and explicit elimination make the difficult transitions reproducible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The recursive-probability node precisely captures the state equations. cnm_h246 supports conditioning, cnm_132 supports the state symmetries, and cnm_090/cnm_089 match the displayed subtraction and substitution.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The supplied exact native links for total probability, reflection, substitution and addition/subtraction elimination are directly relevant. The state-modeling synthesis has no supplied CN alignment and is explained within the solution.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.EE.C.8/8b and A-REI.C.6 overlap through exact algebraic system solving, without graphing. A-REI.C.5's proof of system equivalence is not supplied. Reflection links provide limited isometry overlap, not the full experimental, angle, parallel-line or transformation-function requirements. No US probability alignment is supplied.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Every immediate ID matches a written step. The central state-recursion assessment and supporting conditioning/reflection roles are appropriate, with both elimination procedures justified as method-specific skills.
